text:
Rina: quick check — prototype feedback on the latency panel. p95 line feels noisy when we overlay throughput as an area. options: 1) keep p95 as a crisp stroke + small dot at current, 2) separate mini-chart for throughput, 3) dual-axis with subtle grid. thoughts?
Ben: option 1 is nicest visually. dots help users orient to the latest value. dual-axis confuses some folks in research.
Kai: +1 for stroke + dot. also consider a small percentile selector: users can toggle between p50/p95/p99 right on the sparkline.
Noah: percentile selector = good, but keep it compact. maybe a three-way pill on hover of the sparkline. avoid adding controls to the toolbar.
Priya: hover controls are hard on touch. if we rely on hover, add a persistent compact control in the row for mobile.
Rina: good point. add persistent small control labelled: "pct: p95" that opens the quick selector on click/tap.
Ben: microcopy nit: should it say "pct" or "%ile"? %ile reads weird. maybe just "Percentile: p95" is clearer but longer.
Kai: shorthand accepted in dashboards. proposals: "Percentile: p95" (desktop) and "p95" (mobile compact).
Noah: moving to heatmap: current bins are fixed 50ms which looks wrong for long ranges. need adaptive binning based on total range (e.g., 1min bins for 1h, 5m for 6h, 15m for 24h).
Priya: adaptive bins yes. also add a bin override in advanced settings: users can set custom bin width. hide in advanced to reduce clutter.
Rina: agree. how do we communicate binning in the legend? users asked why colors changed between ranges.
Ben: show a small line: "Bins: 1m" in legend with a tooltip: "Adaptive bin width used for this time range. Click to change."
Kai: tooltip copy: "Bin width influences heatmap resolution and aggregation. Smaller bins = more granular view."
Noah: sampling control: when sampling is on, the heatmap intensity should show a faint diagonal hatch to indicate sampled data. Not an overlay — subtle so it doesn't break pattern recognition.
Priya: we also need a banner that explains sampling in plain language: "Sampling reduces data points to lower query cost. Results remain statistically representative." link to docs.
Rina: good. copy options for banner: 1) "Showing sampled data — learn about sampling", 2) "Sampling active: ~10% of requests displayed". Which is clearer?
Ben: show both: title "Sampling active" and body "Approx. 10% of requests included; sampling preserves latency distribution. Details ->"
Kai: accessibility: ensure the hatch pattern has aria-description and legend entry text for screen readers. Also ensure the hatch has high-contrast option for print.
Noah: for color choices, avoid red/green. propose palette: neutral base for background, p50 = teal (#1ea7a7), p95 = indigo (#3257a8), p99 = purple (#6b3fa0). Test with Deuteranopia sim.
Priya: add a colorblind mode toggle in legend: switches to patterned fills and high-contrast hues. default off but remember preference per-user.
Rina: keyboard/accessibility: can we make the percentile selector keyboard-focusable and cycled with left/right arrows when focused? current prototype requires tab + click.
Ben: yep, implement roving tabindex on pills so arrows move selection. Also support space/enter to toggle.
Kai: analytics ask: track clicks on percentile selector and bin-width changes to see what people use. Noah: i'll add events: heatmap.percentile.changed, heatmap.bin.override.
Priya: printing/export: when exporting PNG/SVG ensure patterns are included and legend text includes bin width and sampling rate. Users export graphs to reports.
Rina: good call. also allow CSV export of underlying histogram buckets with timestamp, bin_start, count, sampled(boolean).
Ben: dev note: backend will need a flag to include sampled boolean per-row. Noah: i'll coordinate with infra.
Kai: final UX asks before we mark ready: 1) persistent percentile pill in the time-row, 2) adaptive binning + bin label in legend, 3) subtle hatch for sampled data + sample banner copy, 4) keyboard arrow nav for pills, 5) colorblind/pattern mode with per-user persistence, 6) export CSV/SVG that includes metadata.
Priya: i'll update figma with the pill, legend variants, and banner copy ("Sampling active — approx. 10% of requests. Learn more").
Noah: i'll add telemetry hooks and backend flag + CSV shape.
Ben: i'll prototype the hatch/print variant and test color palettes.
Kai: i'll write the keyboard interaction spec and hand it to engineering.
design-bot: FYI — follow-up review scheduled Fri 14:00 UTC. Agenda: percentile pill placement, adaptive bin presets, sampling banner copy.
Rina: thanks all, linking prototype in the follow-up. :rocket:
